searchText: <asn_d6> learned about this paper today that could allow us to optimize poly_lincomb() if we ever wanted: https://github.com/zkcrypto/bls12_381/pull/84 i estimated poly_lincomb() currently takes less than 0.3 millisecond to run because 4096 is not that large, but let's be aware of this option <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> How would this speed up poly_lincomb? (re @asn_d6: learned about this paper today that could allow us to optimize poly_lincomb() if we ever wanted: https://github.com/zkcrypto/bls12_381/pull/84 i estimated poly_lincomb() currently takes less than 0.3 millisecond to run because 4096 is not that large, but let's be aware of this option) <asn_d6> the paper shows an algo to do efficient dot products on the field <asn_d6> see https://github.com/zkcrypto/bls12_381/pull/84/files#diff-5761a0b5b725fcd1a29ee1e656cc6b8f1376dc5ec8065263760084cb7e095ed9R426 <asn_d6> poly_lincomb is a bunch of dot products iirc <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> Ah when I read it I interpreted it as how to do an efficient dot product “internally” ie on the limbs of the field element and not on the field element themselves. This in turn for extension fields would speed up G2 operations since it uses field extensions (re @asn_d6: the paper shows an algo to do efficient dot products on the field) <asn_d6> i think u can use it to do proper dot product. eg here is an arkworks unittest: https://github.com/arkworks-rs/algebra/blob/master/test-templates/src/fields.rs#L20 <asn_d6> still havent read the paper fwiw Just in case this is the paper <https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/367>
